conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. You're here because of chest pain and passing out. Can you tell me what happened?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I was drinking and saw a fight. Then I got this chest pain, just like my old heart attacks. It went away for a bit, but came back worse. I passed out, hit my head.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. EMS said your EKG looked concerning, but when we checked, it was mostly the same as before. No new changes except for some Q waves in V5–V6.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So is it my heart again? Feels just like last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked your troponin, which is a blood test for heart damage. It was negative. We’ll repeat it in a few hours to be sure, but right now, it doesn’t look like a new heart attack.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But I passed out. That’s not normal, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, it’s not. We did a CT scan of your head and neck because you hit your head. There’s a scalp hematoma, but no skull fracture or brain bleed. Your spine looks stable too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So why did I pass out?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Given you were drinking and your symptoms started during stress, it’s likely the alcohol played a big role. Your heart rhythm and tests don’t show a dangerous cause.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also did a chest X-ray. It shows some vascular congestion, which can be a sign of heart strain, but no pneumonia or collapsed lung.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had chest pain every other day, but it’s been less since I started taking my meds again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. Your echo from earlier this year showed your heart function is reduced, about 36% ejection fraction. You’ve had stents, but some areas are permanently damaged.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your repeat troponin came back negative again. That’s reassuring. It’s very unlikely you had a heart attack this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel okay now. But my brother just overdosed. My sister’s coming to get me. I need to go.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand, but I strongly recommend you stay. We haven’t optimized your heart meds yet, and you’re still at risk. You haven’t had your beta-blocker, aspirin, or statin since arriving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know, but I can’t stay. I’ll call my PCP and get my meds refilled.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Just know you’re leaving against medical advice. Your chest pain isn’t from a new heart attack, but your heart disease is serious. Please follow up soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks for checking me out.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Before you go, your labs show your kidney and blood counts are normal. Your CPK was a bit high last night, but it’s coming down—likely from the fall or stress, not heart damage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So no heart damage, no brain bleed. Just the alcohol and stress?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s the most likely explanation. But your heart disease is real and needs ongoing care. Please don’t stop your medications again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I won’t. I’ve been trying to stay clean. No heroin, no cocaine. Just had a few drinks this time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a good start. If you’re willing, your PCP can help with addiction support too. This hospitalization could’ve been avoided with better control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll think about it. Just gotta handle this family stuff first.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Understood. Here’s a note for your PCP summarizing everything. Please follow up within a week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll call them tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re alert and walking fine. If anything changes—chest pain, dizziness—come back right away.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks, doc.
